searchText: Is there a slasher running on devnet-8? I've noticed some duplicate blocks: https://light-beaconchain-explorer.dencun-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/0x823a212fd04458c2eed5a576786a3cfa7ad79a6f431448f0f04e60bf7cddd978 https://light-beaconchain-explorer.dencun-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/0xb833820b0e2c4dd3aca522a7b661120ab329e7770ee4bb4e6c8ee00e17a2f1b3 That should be slashed? (Looks like some keys are in multiple clients) These are slashable blocks. But there is no slasher in the network... I've stopped my slasher again to not break the network 😉 https://light-beaconchain-explorer.dencun-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/4d855687aba014a081b02146b5b25eb531a6de6e77d3241535127e2b8ca861c6#proposer-slashings Slashing occured due to our temp setup for replacing the prysm validators while they had trouble syncing, yesterday we deployed a new version of prysm which managed to sync to head, while forgetting to shut down the temp nodes. It was an oversight from my side, and it was nicely catched! Great work <@808969530608451584>. We've had an incident at blobscan.com because of it and we have stopped processing new slots. Could you advice us on what is the best strategy to follow in order to discard forked blocks? What do other block explorer do? https://github.com/Blobscan/blobscan-indexer.rs/issues/19#issuecomment-1693327607 <@514429265001971732> <@808969530608451584> ^ we do not store blocks with uniq numbers I'm storing blocks with block root as primary key. slot is an index, but not unique https://dencun-devnet-8.beaconcha.in/ <a:itshappening:1046791163262271488> <@97774605351010304> where blobs ser? https://tenor.com/view/where-you-at-gif-21177622 zoom in a bit https://discord.com/channels/1020286473938927627/1144605257419198464/1144605945813540978

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: Slashing occured due to our temp setup for replacing the prysm validators while they had trouble syncing, yesterday we deployed a new version of prysm which managed to sync to head, while forgetting to shut down the temp nodes. It was an oversight from my side, and it was nicely catched! Great work <@808969530608451584>.
